info.title: Semester productivity API
info.description: Tasks and calendar events, tenant-scoped and owner-private. Writes are commands that are idempotent and safe to replay from an offline queue; reads are paged. Every operation is authorized by the policy decision point (docs/architecture/0007) and every response carries X-Request-Id and X-Correlation-Id. See docs/API-PLATFORM.md for the conventions this document instantiates.

post.summary: Apply up to 50 commands, in order, each atomically and idempotently.
post.description: Not one transaction: each command commits or fails alone, so one refused command does not strand the rest. The request as a whole is safe to send again after any failure. On the first infrastructure failure the remaining commands are reported `not_attempted`.

200.description: One result per command, in order.

get.summary: The sync pull: every change after a position, tombstones included, in sequence order.

200.description: A page of changes. `seq` is gapless per owner; a jump means a change was missed.

get.summary: Tasks ordered by due date, undated last.

200.description: A page of tasks. For another person's list, only the fields their share allows.

get.summary: One of the caller's own tasks.

304.description: Unchanged since the ETag in If-None-Match.

get.summary: Events overlapping a window, ordered by start.

200.description: A page of events. For another person's calendar, only the fields their share allows.

get.summary: One of the caller's own events.

304.description: Unchanged since the ETag in If-None-Match.

get.summary: The caller's open tasks due and events happening in a window, as one time-ordered list.

200.description: Time-ordered items; `truncated` is true when a cap cut the list.

bearer.description: A session the server validates on every request; the tenant, roles and memberships come from the server's records, never the token's claims.

RequestId.description: Minted per request; never anything a client sent.

CorrelationId.description: The client's X-Correlation-Id if well formed (8-100 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -), otherwise minted. Written to every audit row and event the request causes.

ApiVersion.description: The API major version that served the request.

Purpose.name: X-Semester-Purpose
Purpose.description: Required to read somebody else's data; recorded with the read.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Opaque; a position, never a permission.

OwnerId.name: owner_id
OwnerId.description: Whose data. Defaults to the caller; anyone else's needs a live share grant and X-Semester-Purpose.

ValidationFailed.description: The request is not valid. `details` names each field.

Forbidden.description: The policy decision point refused; `code` is its reason code and `user_action` says what the person can do.

NotFound.description: No such record of the caller's. Another person's record is also not found.

RateLimited.description: Retry after the time in Retry-After.

Unavailable.description: A dependency is down. Reads are safe to retry.

message.description: Kept for clients written before the envelope.

code.description: Stable; a client may switch on it. See x-error-codes.

outcome_known.description: Present only when it is not known whether a change was made.

retry_after_seconds.description: On a 429: seconds to wait. The same number the Retry-After header carries.

commandId.description: Minted on the device when the intent was made. The idempotency key.

clock.description: Hybrid logical clock: wall ms, counter, deviceId (which must equal this command's deviceId). A wall time more than 5 minutes ahead of the server is pulled back.

createdAt.description: When the intent was queued. A command older than 30 days is refused.

id.description: Chosen by the client, so a create can be replayed.

Command.description: Unknown properties are refused, not ignored: owner, tenant, version and source are not the body's to say.

source.description: Only an import may say where an event came from.

CommandResult.description: What happened to one command. `applied`, `superseded` and `duplicate` are all success for the client's queue: remove the command. `rejected` is permanent for this command as sent. `failed` and `not_attempted` mean send it again.

supersededFields.description: Fields a later edit already held; reported, not dropped silently.

not_found.meaning: No such record of the caller's.

internal.meaning: Unexpected; outcome_known is false for a write.

command_expired.meaning: Command queued more than 30 days ago.

source_forbidden.meaning: A person may not name a source.

source_required.meaning: An import must name its source.

idempotency_key_reused.meaning: Command id reused with a different body. As a command result it is `rejected` inside a 200; a single-command endpoint answers 422.

obligation_unsupported.meaning: The decision carried an obligation this service cannot perform, so nothing was shown or changed. On a read it is a 403; on a command it is a `rejected` result inside a 200.

tenant_unverified.meaning: The server did not verify the tenant.

demo_cannot_touch_records.meaning: Demo tenants cannot touch education records.

classification_exceeds_action.meaning: Data more sensitive than the action may touch.

actor_not_person.meaning: Only a signed-in person may read.

grant_missing.meaning: No share grant from the owner for this scope.

grant_not_live.meaning: The grant is expired or revoked.

command_unknown.meaning: Not a verb this entity has.

actor_not_permitted.meaning: This kind of actor may not do this.

service_unbound.meaning: The job is not bound to the tenant.

source_mismatch.meaning: An import may only write imported entries.

not_owner.meaning: Only the owner may change this.
